LeanInfoTheory.Shannon.IsMutuallyIndepen: A finite set S of coordinates is mutually independent under the joint law q if every assignment x to S has joint probability equal to the product over i in S of its one-coordinate marginal probabilities at xᵢ.

A finite collection of variables (Xᵢ) indexed by S is mutually independent under source law p if the joint distribution of their values factors pointwise into the product of their marginal distributions.
LeanInfoTheory.Shannon.isMutuallyIndepen: The empty set of coordinates is mutually independent under every joint probability law.
Every singleton set of coordinates is mutually independent under every joint probability law.
For two distinct indices i and j, mutual independence of the two-member family {Xᵢ,Xⱼ} is equivalent to ordinary independence of Xᵢ and Xⱼ.
With finite coordinate alphabets, any subset S of a mutually independent finite coordinate set T is itself mutually independent.
LeanInfoTheory.Shannon.familyEntropy_eq_: For finite-valued coordinates and a finite set S, the joint entropy of the tuple indexed by S equals the sum of the individual entropies H(Xᵢ) over i in S exactly when the coordinates in S are mutually independent under their joint law.
LeanInfoTheory.Shannon.familyEntropyOf_e: For finite-valued variables defined on a common source, the joint entropy of the tuple indexed by a finite set S is the sum of its individual entropies exactly when those variables are mutually independent under the source law.
LeanInfoTheory.Shannon.sum_mutualInfoOf_: If the finite-valued variables Xᵢ of a finite family are mutually independent, then for any finite-valued Y on the same source, ∑ᵢ I(Xᵢ;Y) ≤ I((Xᵢ)ᵢ;Y).
